newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Power cut in ex-Soviet Georgia to two hours a day.
newsitem.headline: Power cut in ex-Soviet Georgia to two hours a day.

text.p: A water shortage has cut Georgia's already depleted power supply, leaving people in the former Soviet republic with just two hours of electricity a day, Georgia's energy supply company said on Tuesday.
Gruzenergo said the new regime would last throughout the summer months. Spring is already on its way in the mountainous Caucasus state but temperatures still drop below freezing at night.

"Due to the limited volume of water in reservoirs and the limited facilities of Inguri power station, Gruzenergo can only supply the population with electricity for two hours a day, in the evenings," the company said in a statement on television.
Ingurigaz, Georgia's biggest hydroelectric power station, is being prepared for an overhaul.
The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 left Georgia struggling with power supply problems.
Previous limits on power imposed in November cut households' electricity to six hours -- two in the morning and four in the evening.
In February there was a further cut when a Russian-Turkmen join venture stopped sending gas to Georgia saying it was owed money. That problem was overcome but supply problems continued.
Hospitals, bakeries and Tbilisi's underground railway are supplied with electricity on a more or less regular basis, while industries have their own supply schedule.
But homes, even in the capital Tbilisi, are often heated with wood stoves and meals are cooked over kerosene heaters.
